definitions.explanation: A person's given name (as opposed to their family name). Called 'the name below' because in Japanese vertical writing, the given name appears below the family name.

examples.japanese: {下|した}の{名前|なまえ}は{何|なん}ですか。
{下|した}の{名前|なまえ}で{呼|よ}んでもいいですか。
examples.english: May I call you by your first name?

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{親|した}しくないと{下|した}の{名前|なまえ}で{呼|よ}ばないことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: In Japan, people often don't call each other by their first names unless they are close.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
In traditional Japanese vertical writing, names are written with the family name on top and the given name below, hence {下|した}の{名前|なまえ} (the name below).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {名前|なまえ} can mean "given name" in context (as well as "name" in general)
- ファーストネーム (first name — used in international contexts)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Using someone's given name in Japan implies closeness. In most social and professional settings, people use family names with titles like さん. Being invited to use someone's {下|した}の{名前|なまえ} signals a shift to a more personal relationship.
